ROW.COLUMN: (ML/CU) Patterns of Funds Transfers Between Customers and External Entities

An institution's customers may have multiple accounts that span various business lines and are not linked clearly in the institution's transaction or account systems. Patterns of potentially suspicious activity between an institution's customers and other financial institutions, corporations, or individuals may go undetected. Understanding patterns in the client's account and customer's activity with external entities improves the institution's knowledge of its customers and identifies potential areas of concern. This scenario identifies patterns of potentially suspicious activity between internal accounts and customers and external entities, such as high levels of activity or activity that indicates the existence of exclusive relationships between accounts and customers and external entities.

Scenario is realized as one pattern, but this pattern considers focal entity (Customer) - as two parties Originator party and Beneficiary Party, so the pattern will have two sets of datasets - for Originator and Beneficiary parties accordantly. The Originator set of datasets is the default set for scenario.
All alert-generating logic realized in Primary-Rule dataset. This dataset also provides Highlights and Scoring Bindings calculations. No Check-Points used in this pattern.
The Sub-Rules doesn't take part in behavior-detection logic and just provide supporting data for highlights and augmentation Instructions.
The first Sub-Rule is used to provide scenario Supporting Data (Display all electronic funds transaction records that are pertinent to the alert) and the second one to calculate '# of Accts' Highlight - Number of customer accounts involved in all matched transactions.
